awl: Close beside my mother I sat on a rug, with a scrap of buckskin in one hand and an awl in the other.
Oxley, his incredible eyes big and white, "dat dah neygah man ent ha' de graciousness in 'e 'art fuh sen' yo' a ha'penny fuh de chirrun awl dis time?"
Awl yo' go out o' dis house at all howahs o' de night time, like unna is any umans, disregardin' whatevah awdahs dere is.
With an awl she pierced the buckskin, and skillfully threaded it with the white sinew.
Edging between a carpenter's awl and a bag of peas and yams, something ripped a hole in the Bishop's coat.
